# Non Parametric Modelling  

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(survival) # key package for survival analysis
library(ggplot2) # for making plots 
library(ggsurvfit) # nicer survival graphics
library(dplyr)
```

## Doin' it by hand 


## Survival Objects

Turning time to event data into a 'survival' object witht he `Surv()` function. 

```{r}
with(aml, Surv(time = time, event = status))
```

### Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves

Normally this is wrapped in another function. Here we use the `survfit()` function to fit a survival curve. 

```{r}
km <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = aml) 
```

Gives us survival summary stats at various time points.  

```{r}
summary(km)
```

We can specify a time point we care about, for example, 30-day survival. 

```{r}
summary(km, times = 30)
```

Plot a Kaplam-Meier curve 

```{r}
plot(km)
```


We can do this manually with `ggplot2::geom_step()` 

```{r}
km_df <- data.frame(
  time   = km$time,
  surv   = km$surv,
  lower  = km$lower,
  upper  = km$upper
)

ggplot(km_df, aes(x = time, y = surv)) +
  geom_step() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_minimal()

head(km_df)
```


Enhanced plot with `{ggsurvfit}` 

Note: The `survfit2()` function. 

```{r}
survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = aml) |>
  ggsurvfit()
```


```{r}
survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ 1, data = aml) |>
  ggsurvfit() +
  add_confidence_interval() +
  add_risktable() +
  add_quantile(y_value = 0.5, color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.75) +
  scale_ggsurvfit()
```


### Log-Rank Test

Often we want to compare groups. 

```{r}
aml 
```

```{r}
survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ x, data = aml) |>
  ggsurvfit() +
  add_confidence_interval() +
  add_risktable() +
  add_quantile(y_value = 0.5, color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.75) +
  scale_ggsurvfit()
```

```{r}
# Test whether survival differs between groups
logrank_test <- survdiff(Surv(time, status) ~ x, data = aml)

logrank_test
```
